text: Software testing is widely understood as essential to building reliable systems, and it's one of the hardest things to get right.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: A fundamental issue is that tests are good at confirming the behavior a team expects, but the most damaging failures tend to hide in the edge cases no one thought to check during development.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Those blind spots are only growing as AI produces more code that no human has closely reviewed.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Antithesis is a software verification company built around an approach called deterministic simulation testing.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The platform runs a customer software in a fully controlled environment, exploring thousands of different paths through it at runtime.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Crucially, the paths aren't pre-specified and they're not merely the expected cases.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: In this way, it can surface rare, damaging bugs that normal testing would never catch.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Carl Svera is on the red team at Antithesis, and he also leads much of the company's AI strategy.
speaker: SPEAKER_00
